environments.name: Lua Standalone

integration.runtime: PUC Lua 5.4 and 5.1, or LuaJIT 2.1, from the PATH
integration.summary: The `scriptgo` CLI runs resources on a plain Lua interpreter, with no engine. `scriptgo run` ticks the host in simulated or real time and `scriptgo test` runs test scripts; it is the reference host the other environments are compared with.

protection.note: Licence check and signed releases. The host runs plain script, so its operator can read what it loads: no code-secrecy claim.

environments.summary: Runs scripts on plain Lua, with no engine: the place to test them.

capabilityNotes.http: Uses the system curl executable when present.
capabilityNotes.perks: Implemented in the core, over curl. The players are the simulated local ones, so the identifier is local:<name>: for tests and tooling, not for real players.
capabilityNotes.presence: Implemented in the core, over curl. Simulated players with simulated addresses (a run script's `join 2 Bob @203.0.113.7`); the HMAC comes from the system `openssl` executable when it is on the PATH, else presence says it is unavailable and only /link works. Proven by sg_probe_presence on Lua 5.4, 5.1 and LuaJIT against the stub API, with OpenSSL's fingerprints equal to Node's HMAC-SHA256. For tests and tooling, not real players.
capabilityNotes.ui: Notifications are printed to the console.

environments.setupMarkdown:
The standalone host is the `scriptgo` CLI on plain Lua 5.4, 5.1 or LuaJIT. It needs Node.js 22 or
later and a Lua interpreter (`lua`/`luajit` on the `PATH`).

1. Install the package into `./resources`:

   ```bash
   scriptgo add scriptgo//inventory-kit
   ```

2. Run it. Without `--for` or `--script`, the host reads steps from the terminal
   (`cmd 1 /help`, `console <cmd>`, `wait <ms>`, `quit`):

   ```bash
   scriptgo run resources/sg_inventory --search resources --realtime
   ```

3. Privileges, per-resource values and convars come from a JSON file:

   ```json
   {
     "permissions": { "1": ["inventory.give"] },
     "resources": { "sg_inventory": { "slots": 12 } },
     "convars": { "scriptgo_api": "https://api.scriptgo.dev" }
   }
   ```

   ```bash
   scriptgo run resources/sg_inventory --search resources --config config.json
   ```

4. A licensed package: add a deployment on its licence page, then let the host check it. A guarded
   resource starts only on a valid answer, is checked again every ten minutes, and stops when the
   offline grace of its last valid answer ends (72 hours by default):

   ```json
   {
     "convars": { "scriptgo_api": "https://api.scriptgo.dev" },
     "licenses": { "inventory_pro": { "deploymentToken": "sg_dep_...", "package": "kestrel//inventory-pro" } }
   }
   ```

   This is a licence check, not code secrecy: the host runs plain Lua, so its operator can read
   what it loads. A protected (escrow) release arrives as an encrypted bundle; on this host
   `scriptgo escrow load --out <dir>` opens it on your bound server and writes the copy to disk,
   which is licence-only protection.

Storage goes to `.scriptgo-data/storage/` (`--data` to change it). HTTP and licensing use the
system `curl`.

## Player perks

Player perks (`ScriptGo.perks`, `docs/spec/perks.md`): the server asks SCRIPT//GO which of the operator's perks a player has. It needs the server linked to the operator's account (Dashboard, Perks, Servers) and the link's token, a secret, in the host's settings.

```json
{ "convars": { "scriptgo_api": "https://api.scriptgo.dev", "scriptgo_server_token": "sg_srv_..." } }
```

Players here are the simulated ones, so their identifiers are `local:<name>`: this host is for
tests and tooling (`node tools/perks-e2e.mjs`), not for real players. The cache is the file
`storage/scriptgo.perks.json` of the data folder. `scriptgo_perks_poll_seconds` (30) sets how
often the event queue is pulled.
limitations: No rendering: `ui` falls back to console output.
HTTP needs curl on the PATH.

environments.name: LÖVE

integration.summary: A Lua module the game loads, `scriptgo_love.lua`. It runs the core in LÖVE's LuaJIT, ticks it from `love.update` through `sg:update(dt)` and draws notifications with `sg:draw()`. Server and local client share the game process.

protection.note: Licence check and signed releases. The host runs plain script, so its operator can read what it loads: no code-secrecy claim.

environments.summary: Scripts in 2D games made with LÖVE.

capabilityNotes.config: Per-resource values and convars from the config table the game passes.
capabilityNotes.http: curl through io.popen, run in a love.thread worker so frames keep running; unavailable when io.popen or curl is missing. Status and body only, no response headers.
capabilityNotes.perks: Not switched on: a single local player, with no account to tie a purchase to.
capabilityNotes.permissions: Privileges per player id from the config table the game passes.
capabilityNotes.players: Single local player (id 1), the game's own client side.
capabilityNotes.presence: A single local player: nobody to match with a buyer.
capabilityNotes.storage: JSON files in the game's save directory (scriptgo/storage/<key>.json).
capabilityNotes.ui: On-screen toasts drawn by sg:draw(); also logged. Without love.graphics (headless) they are only logged.

environments.setupMarkdown:
1. Copy `scriptgo_love.lua`, `adapter.lua` and `verify.lua` from `sdk/adapters/love2d/` into the
   game (for example `lib/`), and the core `sdk/lua/scriptgo/` next to them as `lib/scriptgo/`.
2. Put resources in a folder of the game, for example `resources/sg_inventory/`.
3. Create the host in `love.load` and drive it from the game's callbacks:

   ```lua
   local scriptgoLove = require("lib.scriptgo_love")
   local sg
   function love.load()
       sg = scriptgoLove.new({
           resources = { "sg_inventory" },          -- dependencies are added too
           search = { "resources" },
           player = { id = 1, name = "Ada" },
           config = { permissions = { ["1"] = { "inventory.give" } } },
       })
   end
   function love.update(dt) sg:update(dt) end
   function love.draw() --[[ the game ]] sg:draw() end
   function love.quit() sg:shutdown() end
   ```

The server side and the local client (player `1`) both run in the game process. Storage goes to
the save directory; HTTP and licensing use `curl` in a `love.thread` worker, so frames keep running.
The layout works from a folder and from a `.love` archive.
limitations: Single-player only: no real network between server and client.
HTTP needs io.popen and a curl executable (on the PATH, or opts.curl).
Measured with LÖVE 11.5 (LuaJIT 2.1) on Windows, as a folder and as a .love archive, through lovec.exe; macOS, Linux, mobile and fused builds are not measured yet.

environments.name: Godot 4

integration.summary: An autoload node, `ScriptGoHost`, creates a Lua state through the lua-gdextension addon, runs the core in it and ticks it from `_process`. Server and local client share the game process.

protection.note: Licence check and signed releases, once the adapter has HTTP. The adapter is script-level, so the operator can read what it loads; a native GDExtension loader would be a later upgrade.

environments.summary: Scripts in Godot 4 games, through a Lua add-on.

capabilityNotes.config: Per-resource values and convars from the config passed to ScriptGoHost.boot.
capabilityNotes.http: Not implemented: no outbound HTTP from resources yet.
capabilityNotes.perks: Needs http, which this adapter does not have.
capabilityNotes.permissions: Privileges per player id from the config passed to ScriptGoHost.boot.
capabilityNotes.players: Single local player (id 1) joined by the scene; ScriptGoHost.join adds simulated ones.
capabilityNotes.presence: Needs http, which this adapter does not have.
capabilityNotes.storage: JSON files at user://scriptgo/storage/<key>.json, written with FileAccess.
capabilityNotes.ui: Queued for the scene (ScriptGoHost.notified signal) and logged; the demo draws them as toasts.

environments.setupMarkdown:
Measured with Godot 4.5.2 and lua-gdextension 0.7.0 (0.8.x needs Godot 4.6).

1. Copy `addons/lua-gdextension` from the lua-gdextension release into the project.
2. Copy `scriptgo_host.gd` and `scriptgo_watchdog.gd` from `sdk/adapters/godot/` to
   `res://addons/scriptgo/` and register them as autoloads, watchdog first:

   ```ini
   [autoload]
   ScriptGoWatchdog="*res://addons/scriptgo/scriptgo_watchdog.gd"
   ScriptGoHost="*res://addons/scriptgo/scriptgo_host.gd"
   ```

3. Import once (`Godot --headless --import --path <project>`, or open the editor) so the
   extension is registered.
4. Point the host at the SDK (`sdk_root`, `--scriptgo-sdk <dir>`, or a copy under
   `res://addons/scriptgo/sdk/`), then boot it:

   ```gdscript
   func _ready():
       ScriptGoHost.boot({ "config": { "permissions": { "1": ["inventory.*"] } } })
       ScriptGoHost.add_search_path(ScriptGoHost.sdk_path + "packages")
       ScriptGoHost.add_resource(ScriptGoHost.sdk_path + "packages/sg_inventory")
       ScriptGoHost.start_all()
       ScriptGoHost.join(1, "Player")
   ```

The host ticks from `_process`. There is no HTTP yet, so licensed packages do not run on Godot.
limitations: Needs the lua-gdextension addon, 0.7.0 for Godot 4.5 (it declares 4.4 as its minimum; the 0.8.x binaries are built for Godot 4.6 and refuse 4.5.2).
No HTTP, so no online license checks.
Single-player only: no real network between server and client.
Measured with Godot 4.5.2 on Windows x86_64, headless and windowed, with the Lua 5.4 and LuaJIT builds of lua-gdextension 0.7.0; exported builds, macOS, Linux, mobile and Web are not measured yet.

environments.name: Luanti

integration.summary: One regular Luanti mod, `scriptgo`, runs the core in the server's Lua and ticks it from a globalstep. It needs no trusted-mod entry; HTTP needs the server owner to list it in `secure.http_mods`.

protection.note: Licence check and signed releases. The host runs plain script, so its operator can read what it loads: no code-secrecy claim.

environments.summary: Scripts on Luanti (formerly Minetest) servers, through one regular mod.

capabilityNotes.commands: Resource commands are ordinary chat commands.
capabilityNotes.events: Server side only; client scripts do not run (Luanti mods are server-side).
capabilityNotes.http: Needs the mod listed in secure.http_mods by the server owner.
capabilityNotes.perks: Not switched on: the core implements perks over http and the player identifier, which this adapter has, but it has not been wired or run here.
capabilityNotes.permissions: server or scriptgo_admin privilege, then the grants in <world>/scriptgo.json.
capabilityNotes.players: Player names get session-stable integer ids; identifier is luanti:<name>.
capabilityNotes.presence: The adapter answers a player's address (core.get_player_ip), but presence is not switched on: perks are not, Luanti has no HMAC (only hashes), and a player name is not an account other servers share.
capabilityNotes.ui: Notifications are sent as chat messages.

environments.setupMarkdown:
1. Build the mod, optionally with resources bundled in:

   ```bash
   node sdk/adapters/luanti/build.mjs --with sdk/packages/sg_inventory --with sdk/packages/sg_eventbus
   ```

2. Copy `dist/luanti/scriptgo/` into the server's `mods/` folder and enable it for the world
   (`load_mod_scriptgo = true` in `world.mt`). It is a regular mod: it needs no entry in
   `secure.trusted_mods`.
3. Put further resources in `<world>/scriptgo/resources/<name>/`. Every resource with
   `auto_start true` starts with the server, dependencies first.
4. Optional `<world>/scriptgo.json`:

   ```json
   {
     "resources": { "sg_inventory": { "slots": 30 } },
     "convars": { "scriptgo_api": "https://api.scriptgo.dev" },
     "permissions": { "alice": ["command.giveitem"] }
   }
   ```

Only the server side runs. HTTP, and so online license checks, needs the mod listed in
`secure.http_mods` by the server owner.
limitations: No client side.
HTTP, and so online license checks, only when the server owner allows it.
Verified headless on Luanti 5.18.0 (LuaJIT); paths that need a connected player are not yet covered by a run.

environments.name: OPEN//77
environments.platformRulesNote: A script is your own code. CD PROJEKT RED's own rules cover the game's content.

integration.runtime: OPEN//77's own Lua 5.4 runtime, on its dedicated server and game client
integration.summary: OPEN//77 runs its own Lua runtime with the same resource shape. `scriptgo pack --target open77` adapts a package to it: a generated `open77.lua` manifest, the package's files, and a three-file shim (shared, server, client), loaded first, that maps `ScriptGo.*` onto OPEN//77's `Open77.*` API. The packed manifest asks only for the permissions the package's capabilities need.

protection.note: Code escrow, an opt-in server feature: a protected release is decrypted in memory, with a key released to the licensed server only. The operator of the machine can still inspect their own process; that takes real effort and the copy is traceable.

environments.summary: Scripts on OPEN//77 servers, packed as regular OPEN//77 resources.

capabilityNotes.config: Server side: convar <resource>:<key>, then the resource's tunables.
capabilityNotes.http: Server side, through Open77.http.request (permission http.request). Off until the operator sets server.jsonc http.enabled and lists each host in http.allowedHosts; redirects are never followed.
capabilityNotes.licensing: Server side, over Open77.http.request to the scriptgo_api convar; the operator allows the API host.
capabilityNotes.perks: Server side, in the shim: the core's perks module over Open77.http.request (the operator allows the API host) and Open77.players.identifier. The shim is packed per resource, so each resource that uses perks polls on its own; the cache is kept in the resource's kvp.
capabilityNotes.permissions: Server side: the server ACL (Open77.acl.isAllowed, permission acl.read).
capabilityNotes.presence: Server side, in the shim: the /link command works over Open77.http.request. Presence reporting reads Open77.players.endpoint (permission players.identity.sensitive, requested in the packed manifest only for a resource that declares presence) and needs an HMAC-SHA256 native, which OPEN//77 build 2.50.0+op77.208 does not have: until it does, presence says it is unavailable and only /link works. One resource per server should declare it. Ran on an OPEN//77 server (sg_probe_presence): the shim loads, the permission is accepted, status says no HMAC; no game client was connected, so /link has not been typed by a real player.
capabilityNotes.storage: Open77.kvp on both sides, values stored as JSON text.
capabilityNotes.ui: Server: Open77.notifications; client: the open77_notifications package.

environments.setupMarkdown:
The CLI packs a resource with a small shim that maps `ScriptGo.*` onto `Open77.*`:

```bash
scriptgo pack my_resource --target open77 --out dist
# dist/open77/my_resource/ is a resource folder OPEN//77 loads as is
```

The packed manifest asks for exactly the OPEN//77 permissions the resource's capabilities need.
A resource that uses `http` or `licensing` also needs the operator to allow the API host in
`server.jsonc`:

```jsonc
"http": { "enabled": true, "allowedHosts": ["api.scriptgo.dev"] },
"convars": { "scriptgo_api": "https://api.scriptgo.dev" }
```

`scriptgo_api` defaults to `https://api.scriptgo.dev`: set it only to use another SCRIPT//GO API (a
local one in development), and allow that host instead.

The license key goes in the `<resource>:license_key` convar, never in the resource folder.

## Protected (escrowed) scripts

Code escrow is an opt-in, default-off feature of the OPEN//77 server. The server decrypts a
protected release through a native library: the key stays in native memory and the plain code never
reaches the disk. Only server scripts are encrypted; shared and client scripts go to game clients,
so they stay readable.

1. Install the release still encrypted:

   ```bash
   scriptgo escrow install <name>-<version>.escrow.zip --target open77 --out <resources folder> --trusted-signer <key>
   ```

2. Put the deployment token of that licence in `.open77/escrow-tokens/<resource>.token`, one line,
   never in `server.jsonc` or in the resource folder.
3. Turn `resourceEscrow` on in `server.jsonc` and put the escrow adapter next to the server, built
   with `ScriptGo.Escrow` from this SDK's releases. Without the adapter, the server refuses an
   escrowed resource with `adapter_missing`.

The full procedure is in `sdk/adapters/open77/escrow/README.md`. The operator of the machine can
still inspect their own process; that takes real effort, and the copy is traceable.

## Player perks

Player perks (`ScriptGo.perks`, `docs/spec/perks.md`): the server asks SCRIPT//GO which of the operator's perks a player has. It needs the server linked to the operator's account (Dashboard, Perks, Servers) and the link's token, a secret, in the host's settings.

```jsonc
"http": { "enabled": true, "allowedHosts": ["api.scriptgo.dev"] },
"convars": { "scriptgo_api": "https://api.scriptgo.dev", "scriptgo_server_token": "sg_srv_..." }
```

Nothing about payments is in OPEN//77: `scriptgo pack` puts the portable perks module into the
resource's server shim, and that Lua calls SCRIPT//GO over the HTTP the operator allowed. A player is
`Open77.players.identifier(id)`, the account the OPEN//77 master verified; a masterless
`devLocalAuth` server gives its players no identifier, so they have no perk there. The cache is the
key `scriptgo.perks` of the resource's kvp. Each resource that uses perks pulls the event queue on
its own.
limitations: Outbound HTTP, and so licensing and perks, needs the server operator to allow the SCRIPT//GO API host; the client side has no HTTP.
The client side has no wall clock: ScriptGo.time.now() is nil there.
Real runs cover the server side; the client side has not been run in a verification yet.

environments.name: Neovim

integration.summary: An ordinary Neovim plugin. `setup()` starts the core in Neovim's LuaJIT, a libuv timer ticks it on the main loop, and `:ScriptGo <command>` runs resource commands. Server and local client run in the editor.

protection.note: Licence check and signed releases. The host runs plain script, so its operator can read what it loads: no code-secrecy claim.

environments.summary: Scripts inside the Neovim editor, as an ordinary plugin.

capabilityNotes.commands: Resource commands are typed as :ScriptGo <command> and run as the local player.
capabilityNotes.config: Per-resource values and convars from the config passed to setup().
capabilityNotes.http: curl through vim.system (Neovim 0.10 or later), asynchronous so the editor never waits; unavailable without curl. Status and body only, no response headers.
capabilityNotes.perks: Not applicable: an editor has no players to sell a perk to.
capabilityNotes.permissions: Privileges per player id from the config passed to setup().
capabilityNotes.players: Single local player (id 1), the person at the keyboard.
capabilityNotes.presence: Not applicable: an editor has no players to match.
capabilityNotes.ui: Notifications go to vim.notify; a headless run only logs them.

environments.setupMarkdown:
Needs Neovim 0.10 or later (measured on 0.12.6) and `curl` for licensed packages.

1. Add `sdk/adapters/neovim/` to Neovim as a plugin. Inside the SDK checkout it finds the core by
   itself; elsewhere copy `sdk/lua/scriptgo/` to `lua/scriptgo_nvim/core/` in the plugin, or set
   `vim.g.scriptgo_core`. With lazy.nvim:

   ```lua
   {
     dir = "~/scriptgo/sdk/adapters/neovim",
     config = function()
       require("scriptgo_nvim").setup({
         search = { vim.fn.expand("~/scriptgo/resources") },
         resources = { "sg_inventory" },
         config = { permissions = { ["1"] = { "*" } } },
       })
     end,
   }
   ```

2. Use it from the editor:

   ```vim
   :ScriptGo status
   :ScriptGo giveitem 1 water 2
   :ScriptGo log
   ```

The server side and the local client (you, player `1`) run inside the editor, ticked by a timer on
the main loop. Notifications go to `vim.notify`; storage to `stdpath("data")/scriptgo/storage`.
limitations: Single user: no real network between server and client.
HTTP, and so online license checks, needs curl and Neovim 0.10 or later.
Measured with Neovim 0.12.6 (LuaJIT 2.1) on Windows, headless (nvim --headless --clean -l); macOS, Linux and older Neovim releases are not measured yet.

environments.name: CC: Tweaked (Minecraft)
environments.platformRulesNote: The Minecraft EULA lets you do what you want with your mods "as long as you don't sell them for money" (minecraft.net/en-us/eula).

integration.runtime: CC: Tweaked 1.121.0 on a Minecraft 1.20.1 Fabric server (Cobalt, Lua 5.2)
integration.summary: A program on one ComputerCraft computer, which the CC: Tweaked mod adds to a Fabric server. It runs the core in the computer's Lua 5.2 VM, ticked by a CC timer every server tick; the server and client sides both run on that computer.

protection.note: No licence check in this adapter, so a package runs there without one. Releases are still signed.

environments.summary: Scripts on a ComputerCraft computer in a Minecraft: Java Edition world, through the CC: Tweaked mod. Not an official Minecraft product; not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft.

capabilityNotes.commands: Typed at the computer's sg> prompt; they run as the terminal player.
capabilityNotes.config: Per-resource values from /scriptgo/config.json; convars from config.json, then the computer's settings.
capabilityNotes.events: Server and client run on the same computer; network events between them are looped back through the value codec.
capabilityNotes.http: CC: Tweaked's asynchronous http API. The server owner decides in computercraft-server.toml whether it is on and which hosts answer ([[http.rules]]; private and local addresses are denied by default). Redirects are not followed.
capabilityNotes.licensing: Not implemented: this adapter was built without a licence check, after the Minecraft Usage Guidelines, which allow a mod only if it "cannot be used to directly or indirectly verify whether a player owns or has access to out-of-game content, products, or services that affect in-game features and functions" (minecraft.net/en-us/usage-guidelines).
capabilityNotes.perks: Not implemented, for the reason given for licensing.
capabilityNotes.players: One player: the person at the computer's terminal (id 1). The world's other players are not visible.
capabilityNotes.presence: Not implemented, for the reason given for licensing.
capabilityNotes.storage: JSON files on the computer's own disk (/scriptgo/data/<key>.json), within the server's computer_space_limit (1 MB by default).
capabilityNotes.ui: Notifications are lines on the computer's terminal.

environments.setupMarkdown:
Needs a Minecraft: Java Edition server you own or run, with [Fabric](https://fabricmc.net) and the
[CC: Tweaked](https://tweaked.cc) mod (measured with Minecraft 1.20.1, Fabric loader 0.20.1, Fabric API
0.92.12 and CC: Tweaked 1.121.0). Not an official Minecraft product. Not approved by or associated
with Mojang or Microsoft. Not affiliated with the CC: Tweaked developers.

**The platform's own rules.** The [Minecraft EULA](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/eula) lets you do
what you want with mods you create "as long as you don't sell them for money / try to make money from
them". SCRIPT//GO does not enforce a platform's rules: you answer to the platform's rights holder for
what you run on your server.

**No licence check.** This adapter has none. It was built without one after the
[Minecraft Usage Guidelines](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/usage-guidelines), which allow a mod
only if it "cannot be used to directly or indirectly verify whether a player owns or has access to
out-of-game content, products, or services that affect in-game features and functions". A package
runs here without a licence check.

1. Build the computer's files, with your resources:

   ```sh
   node sdk/adapters/cctweaked/build.mjs --with path/to/my_resource --startup
   ```

   This writes `dist/cctweaked/computer/`: the SCRIPT//GO core, the adapter, the `sg` program and
   your resources. Optional: `scriptgo/config.json` there sets permissions, config and convars:

   ```json
   { "permissions": { "1": ["*"] }, "resources": { "my_resource": { "greeting": "hi" } } }
   ```

2. Place a computer in the world, note its id (`id` in its shell), stop the server and copy the
   folder's contents into `<world>/computercraft/computer/<id>/`. The default disk of a computer is
   1 MB (`computer_space_limit` in `<world>/serverconfig/computercraft-server.toml`).

3. Start the server and use the computer: with `--startup` it runs SCRIPT//GO at boot; otherwise
   type `scriptgo/sg`. At the `sg>` prompt, resource commands run as the person at the terminal
   (player `1`); `status`, `log`, `restart <name>` and `exit` drive the host.

Running a Minecraft server, including the headless one `scriptgo verify --env cctweaked` starts,
means accepting the [Minecraft EULA](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/eula): the operator must accept
it themselves (`eula=true` in the server's `eula.txt`, or `--accept-minecraft-eula` on a verify run).
SCRIPT//GO never accepts it for anyone.

HTTP, when a resource uses it, goes through CC: Tweaked's `http` API, so the server's
`computercraft-server.toml` decides whether it is on and which hosts answer (`[[http.rules]]`; local
and private addresses are denied by default).
limitations: Experimental: one real server run so far, the conformance probe (35 of 35 checks). The official kits fail there only because they do not declare cctweaked yet. Each run needs the operator's own acceptance of the Minecraft EULA.
No licence check in this adapter (see the licensing note). What the Minecraft EULA says about paid mods is the platform's own rule, shown as the platform note.
Not an official Minecraft product. Not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft. Not affiliated with the CC: Tweaked developers.
Lua 5.2 (Cobalt VM): no // or bitwise operators (use bit32), no collectgarbage.
Everything runs on one computer: code that runs for about 7 seconds without yielding is stopped by CC: Tweaked ("Too long without yielding").
Pinned for runs: Minecraft 1.20.1, Fabric loader 0.20.1, CC: Tweaked 1.121.0. Other versions are not measured.
Fast tests use the cc-core harness (CC: Tweaked's own core and Lua VM without Minecraft); those runs are an emulator and do not count as verification.

environments.name: .NET kit

integration.summary: An embedded host kit: `ScriptGo.Host`, a .NET 10 library that a C# engine or server references and ticks from its own loop. It runs Lua 5.4 (KeraLua) and JavaScript or TypeScript (Jint) side by side, one VM per resource side and language. Its console host, `scriptgo-dotnet`, runs the verification.

protection.note: Code escrow: the kit's compiled loader decrypts in memory with a key released to this server only. The operator of the machine can still inspect their own process; that takes real effort and the copy is traceable.

environments.summary: A library that C# engines and servers embed to run Lua, TypeScript and JavaScript scripts.

capabilityNotes.http: HttpClient off the host thread; the answer is delivered on the next tick.
capabilityNotes.licensing: Through the kit's HTTP, against the SCRIPT//GO API (checked against the API schemas by --stub-api).
capabilityNotes.perks: Lua guests: the kit runs the core's perks module in the guest, over IHostHttp and IHostPlayers.Identifier. JavaScript and TypeScript guests do not have it yet (capability_unavailable).
capabilityNotes.players: The console host simulates players; an integrating engine supplies its own through IHostPlayers.
capabilityNotes.presence: Lua guests: the kit runs the core's presence module over IHostHttp, IHostPlayers.Identifier and the optional IHostPlayerAddresses, with .NET's HMACSHA256. JavaScript and TypeScript guests do not have it (capability_unavailable). Proven in the kit's tests with a fake API (reports, removal, /link), and by sg_probe_presence through the kit's runner against the stub API, the fingerprint equal to Node's HMAC-SHA256. One Lua resource per host should declare it.
capabilityNotes.storage: The integrator's IHostStorage; the console host keeps it in memory, or in JSON files with --data.
capabilityNotes.ui: The console host writes notifications to its log; an engine implements IHostUi.

environments.setupMarkdown:
The .NET kit is a library (`ScriptGo.Host`, .NET 10) that a C# engine or server embeds, plus a
console host (`scriptgo-dotnet`) that runs and verifies resources without an engine. It runs Lua
resources (Lua 5.4 through KeraLua) and TypeScript or JavaScript resources (Jint). It is
experimental and has been measured on Windows x64 only.

1. Install the .NET 10 SDK. The `scriptgo` CLI finds it on the `PATH`, in `DOTNET_ROOT`, in the
   default install folder, or through `--dotnet <path>` / `SCRIPTGO_DOTNET`.

2. Verify a resource on the kit. The first run builds the console host; TypeScript entries are
   compiled with esbuild into a temporary copy (the source folder is not changed):

   ```bash
   scriptgo verify resources/sg_inventory --env dotnet
   scriptgo verify resources/my_ts_resource --env dotnet --lang ts
   ```

3. Run resources with the console host. It loads compiled TypeScript (`x.ts.js` next to `x.ts`),
   which a `scriptgo pack` archive contains:

   ```bash
   dotnet sdk/dotnet/ScriptGo.Host.Standalone/bin/Release/net10.0/scriptgo-dotnet.dll run resources/sg_inventory --search resources --for 2000
   ```

4. Privileges, per-resource values and convars come from a JSON file (`--config`), as in the
   standalone host; `--data <dir>` keeps storage in JSON files instead of memory:

   ```json
   {
     "permissions": { "1": ["inventory.give"] },
     "resources": { "sg_inventory": { "slots": 12 } },
     "convars": { "scriptgo_api": "https://api.scriptgo.dev" }
   }
   ```

To embed the kit in an engine, see `sdk/dotnet/README.md`.

## Player perks

Player perks (`ScriptGo.perks`, `docs/spec/perks.md`): the server asks SCRIPT//GO which of the operator's perks a player has. It needs the server linked to the operator's account (Dashboard, Perks, Servers) and the link's token, a secret, in the host's settings.

```json
{ "convars": { "scriptgo_api": "https://api.scriptgo.dev", "scriptgo_server_token": "sg_srv_..." } }
```

Lua guests have `ScriptGo.perks`: the kit runs the portable perks module in the guest, over
`IHostHttp` and `IHostPlayers.Identifier` (the engine's own account id). JavaScript and TypeScript
guests do not have it yet: `capability_unavailable:perks@dotnet`. The cache is kept in memory.
limitations: TypeScript must be compiled first (scriptgo pack or scriptgo verify do it with esbuild); the kit loads x.ts.js next to x.ts.
The JavaScript memory quota bounds what one entry allocates on the host thread, not the live heap (Jint has no per-engine heap limit).
Server and client run in one process: no real network between them.
C# guests are not available yet (planned).
Measured with .NET 10 on Windows x64 only.

capabilityNotes.config: Per-resource values and convars from scriptgo.json in the plugin's data folder.
capabilityNotes.events: Server side only: Hytale plugins run on the server and players install nothing.
capabilityNotes.http: java.net.http, off until the operator lists hosts in scriptgo.json http.allowedHosts; redirects are never followed.
capabilityNotes.logging: The server log, through the plugin's logger.
capabilityNotes.perks: Not switched on: the core implements perks over http and the player identifier, which this adapter has, but it has not been wired or run here.

integration.summary: One server addon, `scriptgo`, carries the core and runs it in the server's GLua, ticked on the `Think` hook. `scriptgo pack --target garrysmod` turns each package into its own addon.

protection.note: Licence check and signed releases. The host runs plain script, so its operator can read what it loads: no code-secrecy claim.

environments.summary: Scripts on Garry's Mod servers (roleplay, sandbox, game modes), through one server addon.

capabilityNotes.commands: Chat /name or !name for commands a resource registered; console `scriptgo run <line>`.
capabilityNotes.config: data/scriptgo/config.json per resource; GetConvar reads its convars, then the server's convars.
capabilityNotes.events: Server side only; client scripts do not run yet. The scheduler ticks on the Think hook, every server frame.
capabilityNotes.http: The engine's asynchronous HTTP(): any method, status, body and headers. Loopback and private addresses need srcds -allowlocalhttp.
capabilityNotes.licensing: Over HTTP() to the scriptgo_api convar (default https://api.scriptgo.dev).
capabilityNotes.perks: Not switched on: the core implements perks over http and the player identifier, which this adapter has, but it has not been wired or run here.
capabilityNotes.permissions: superadmin, then CAMI (privilege scriptgo.<name>, for ULX, SAM and other admin mods), then grants by usergroup, SteamID64 or SteamID in data/scriptgo/config.json.
capabilityNotes.players: The player's UserID() is its id; identifier steam:<SteamID64>, bot:<id> for bots. Join and drop come from PlayerInitialSpawn and player_disconnect.
capabilityNotes.presence: The adapter answers a player's address (Player:IPAddress()), but presence is not switched on: perks are not, and GLua has no HMAC (util.SHA256 only).

environments.setupMarkdown:
1. Build the runtime addon, optionally with resources bundled in:

   ```bash
   node sdk/adapters/garrysmod/build.mjs --with sdk/packages/sg_inventory --with sdk/packages/sg_eventbus
   ```

   or pack each resource as its own addon (the runtime addon comes with it, `--no-runtime` leaves
   it out):

   ```bash
   scriptgo pack sdk/packages/sg_inventory --target garrysmod   # -> dist/garrysmod/scriptgo_sg_inventory/ + dist/garrysmod/scriptgo/
   ```

2. Copy the folders into the server's `garrysmod/addons/` and restart the map. Every resource with
   `auto_start true` starts once the map has loaded, dependencies first. Server owners can also put
   resources in `garrysmod/data/scriptgo/resources/<name>/`.
3. Optional `garrysmod/data/scriptgo/config.json`:

   ```json
   {
     "resources": { "sg_inventory": { "slots": 30 } },
     "permissions": { "admin": ["command.giveitem"], "76561198000000000": ["shop.*"] }
   }
   ```

   Permissions also come from superadmin and, with an admin mod such as ULX or SAM, from the CAMI
   privileges `scriptgo.<name>`.
4. Licensed packages call the SCRIPT//GO API at `https://api.scriptgo.dev`. To use another one (a
   local API in development), set `scriptgo_api` in `server.cfg`
   (`scriptgo_api "http://localhost:4100"`). An API on a loopback or private address also needs
   `-allowlocalhttp` on the srcds command line.

Only the server side runs: client scripts are not executed yet. Keep `sv_hibernate_think 1` if
resources must keep running while the server is empty. Resource commands are typed in chat as
`/name` or `!name`; the server console has `scriptgo`, `scriptgo restart <name>` and
`scriptgo run <command line>`.

To check a resource on your own server folder (a copy, not a live server):

```bash
scriptgo verify <resourceDir> --env garrysmod --gmod-server <folder with srcds.exe>
```

The server itself is the free Garry's Mod Dedicated Server (Steam app 4020), installed with
SteamCMD and an anonymous login: `steamcmd +force_install_dir <dir> +login anonymous +app_update 4020 validate +quit`.
On Windows it takes about 7 GB.
limitations: Server side only: client scripts (HUD, Derma) need a game client and are not run yet.
Verified on the Windows dedicated server (public branch, 32-bit LuaJIT 2.0.4 and 64-bit LuaJIT 2.1), headless, with a bot as the player; Linux servers and real Steam players are not measured yet.
An empty server hibernates and stops ticking unless sv_hibernate_think is 1.
CAMI is implemented but not yet run with a real admin mod.

environments.name: Rust (Oxide/Carbon)
environments.platformRulesNote: The developer allows selling mods you own.

integration.runtime: Rust dedicated server with Oxide or Carbon; KeraLua (Lua 5.4)
integration.summary: One C# plugin, `ScriptGo.cs`, the same file for Oxide and Carbon. Rust's plugin frameworks no longer run Lua, so the plugin loads a small bridge that runs the core in a KeraLua (Lua 5.4) VM, ticked by a framework timer.

protection.note: Code escrow: the compiled bridge next to the plugin has the native loader decrypt in memory, with a key released to this server only. It is off until the operator turns it on in the plugin config. Measured on Windows servers with Oxide and with Carbon, and on a Linux server with Oxide in a container. The operator of the machine can still inspect their own process; that takes real effort and the copy is traceable.

environments.summary: Scripts on Rust servers, through one Oxide or Carbon plugin.

capabilityNotes.commands: Chat commands (/name) through OnPlayerCommand; the console command scriptgo manages resources.
capabilityNotes.config: The plugin config (ScriptGo.json): resources.<name> and convars. Rust's own server convars are not exposed.
capabilityNotes.events: Server side only: Rust has no client-side plugins. Lua 5.4 runs in KeraLua inside the plugin.
capabilityNotes.http: Oxide/Carbon web requests. Response headers are not available; httpAllowedHosts can limit the hosts.
capabilityNotes.licensing: Over the plugin's web requests, to the scriptgo_api convar.
capabilityNotes.perks: Implemented in the core, over the plugin's web requests; the player is steam:<steamid64>. The cache is kept in the plugin's data files. Proven in the bridge's .NET test process with fake services; not run on a Rust server yet.
capabilityNotes.permissions: Oxide permissions: privilege p is scriptgo.p; scriptgo.admin holds every privilege.
capabilityNotes.players: BasePlayer. Steam ids get integer ids that stay stable while the plugin is loaded; identifier is steam:<steamid64>.
capabilityNotes.presence: Implemented in the core: the address is the player's connection address (net.connection.ipaddress), the HMAC is .NET's HMACSHA256 in the bridge. Proven in the bridge's .NET test process with fake services; not run on a Rust server with a connected player yet.
capabilityNotes.ui: Notifications are sent as colored chat lines.

environments.setupMarkdown:
These steps were followed on real Windows dedicated servers, one with Oxide and one with Carbon
(2026-11-10: the conformance probe and the escrow chain pass on both, see README.md, "What has
run"). On Linux, Oxide was run the same way in a container (`tools/rust-server-linux.ps1`); Carbon
on Linux and a start through `runds.sh` are written from the documentation and untested.

1. Build the plugin files, optionally with resources:

   ```bash
   node sdk/adapters/rust/build.mjs --with sdk/packages/sg_inventory --with sdk/packages/sg_eventbus
   ```

   `dist/rust/` mirrors the server's root folder. The build needs the .NET SDK.

2. Install Oxide or Carbon on the server, not both. Then copy from `dist/rust/` into the server root:

   | File | Where |
   |---|---|
   | `ScriptGo.Bridge.dll`, `KeraLua.dll` | `RustDedicated_Data/Managed/` |
   | `lua54.dll` (Windows) or `liblua54.so` (Linux) | `RustDedicated_Data/Plugins/x86_64/` |
   | `ScriptGo.cs` | `oxide/plugins/` for Oxide, `carbon/plugins/` for Carbon |

   The plugin loads the two DLLs through its `// Reference: ScriptGo.Bridge` line. After you replace
   either DLL, restart the server: reloading the plugin keeps the old ones loaded.

3. Put each resource in `oxide/data/ScriptGo/resources/<name>/` (Carbon: `carbon/data/...`). Every
   resource with `auto_start true` starts when the server is up, dependencies first.

4. Edit the plugin config, `oxide/config/ScriptGo.json` (Carbon: `carbon/configs/ScriptGo.json`).
   The plugin writes it on its first load.

   ```json
   {
     "resources": { "sg_inventory": { "slots": 30 } },
     "convars": { "scriptgo_api": "https://api.scriptgo.dev" },
     "httpAllowedHosts": ["api.scriptgo.dev"],
     "start": null
   }
   ```

5. Grant privileges with Oxide permissions. Every SCRIPT//GO privilege `p` becomes `scriptgo.p`:

   ```text
   oxide.grant user <steamid> scriptgo.command.giveitem      (Carbon: c.grant user ...)
   oxide.grant group admin scriptgo.admin                    (every privilege, and the scriptgo command)
   ```

Only the server side runs: Rust has no client-side plugins. Check what is running with
`scriptgo status` in the server console.

## Encrypted (escrowed) packages

Optional and off by default. Proven on Windows servers with Oxide and with Carbon, and on a Linux
server with Oxide in a container. Read
"Escrow" in README.md first: it is deterrence, licence binding, revocation and traceability, not a
guarantee, and the operator of the machine can ultimately recover what their own server runs.

1. Build with the native escrow library, from a build of `sdk/native` (`build.ps1` on Windows,
   `build-linux.ps1` for Linux x64):

   ```bash
   node sdk/adapters/rust/build.mjs --native sdk/native/dist
   ```

   `SCRIPTGO_NATIVE_DIR` works too. Copy `scriptgo.dll` (on Linux `libscriptgo.so`) from
   `dist/rust/RustDedicated_Data/Plugins/x86_64/` to the same folder of the server, next to
   `lua54`. Without it the plugin still runs clear packages and refuses an escrowed one with
   `native_missing`.

2. Put the escrowed resource in `oxide/data/ScriptGo/resources/<name>/` as the creator's bundle
   unzipped (`escrow.json`, `payload.enc`, the clear files) plus a one-line stub at the path of
   each encrypted script the manifest lists. README.md, "On disk", shows the stub.

3. Put the deployment token of that resource on this server in
   `oxide/data/ScriptGo/escrow/tokens/<name>.token` (Carbon: `carbon/data/...`), one line. It is a
   secret: keep the folder readable by the server's account only, and out of backups you share.

4. Turn escrow on in the plugin config and reload the plugin:

   ```json
   "escrow": { "enabled": true, "master": "https://api.scriptgo.dev", "trustedSigners": [] }
   ```

   The first escrowed start creates this server's identity in
   `oxide/data/ScriptGo/escrow/identity.key` and logs its public key. The licence is bound to it on
   the first key request. Back the file up: without it the server has to be bound again.

5. `scriptgo status` shows each escrowed resource: `pending_key` while the key is on its way, then
   `started  [escrow licensed, ...]`, or `failed  [escrow <reason>: ...]`. The reasons are listed in
   README.md, "Refusals". After fixing the cause, `scriptgo start <name>` asks the key service again.

## Player perks

Player perks (`ScriptGo.perks`, `docs/spec/perks.md`): the server asks SCRIPT//GO which of the operator's perks a player has. It needs the server linked to the operator's account (Dashboard, Perks, Servers) and the link's token, a secret, in the host's settings. In the plugin's configuration, next to `scriptgo_api`:

```json
"convars": { "scriptgo_api": "https://api.scriptgo.dev", "scriptgo_server_token": "sg_srv_..." }
```

A player is `steam:<steamid64>`. The cache goes to the plugin's data files (`scriptgo.perks`). This
is unit-tested in the bridge with fake services; it has not been run on a Rust server with a
connected player.
limitations: Measured on Windows dedicated servers with Oxide and with Carbon, and on a Linux dedicated server with Oxide in a container, with no player connected: the conformance probe and the escrow chain. What a connected player triggers (chat commands, permissions of real Steam ids) is not measured, nor Carbon on Linux.
No client side.
KeraLua's native Lua 5.4 (lua54.dll or liblua54.so) must be installed in RustDedicated_Data/Plugins/x86_64.
HTTP responses carry no headers.

environments.name: BeamMP
environments.platformRulesNote: Neither BeamNG nor BeamMP publishes a rule on selling mods.
environments.blockedOn: Waiting for a server key: BeamMP-Server does not start without an AuthKey from the BeamMP Keymaster, which the server owner requests.

integration.summary: One BeamMP server plugin, `scriptgo`, runs the core in the plugin's own Lua 5.3 state, ticked by a 25 ms event timer. `scriptgo pack --target beammp` builds it with the package and its dependencies.

protection.note: Licence check and signed releases, once the adapter has passed a run on a real server. The server plugin is plain Lua, so the operator can read what it loads: no code-secrecy claim.

environments.summary: Scripts on BeamMP servers (BeamNG.drive multiplayer), through one server plugin.

capabilityNotes.commands: Chat commands (/name ...; the line is not broadcast) and the server console, where they run as the console.
capabilityNotes.events: Server side only: the plugin runs no client scripts, and TriggerClientEvent answers network_unavailable.
capabilityNotes.http: curl started in the background through os.execute and polled each tick, so a request never blocks the plugin; needs curl on the server's PATH. BeamMP's own Http.CreateConnection has no POST and drops the response.
capabilityNotes.licensing: Over the same curl path, to the scriptgo_api convar.
capabilityNotes.perks: Not switched on: the core implements perks over http and the player identifier, which this adapter has, but it has not been wired or run here.
capabilityNotes.permissions: Grants in scriptgo.json, by beammp:<account id>, or by name for players logged in to BeamMP: BeamMP has no server-side roles.
capabilityNotes.players: MP.GetPlayers and the join and disconnect events. BeamMP id n is SCRIPT//GO player n + 1 (0 is the console); identifier is beammp:<account id>, beammp-guest:<name> for guests.
capabilityNotes.presence: The adapter answers a player's address (MP.GetPlayerIdentifiers(pid).ip), but presence is not switched on: perks are not, and BeamMP's Lua has no HMAC.
capabilityNotes.storage: JSON files in the plugin's data/storage folder (scriptgo.json dataDir), replaced atomically.
capabilityNotes.ui: MP.SendNotification (a toast in the BeamMP client); its display is not verified, as no game client runs here.

limitations: Not verified on a real server yet: BeamMP-Server (3.9.3) refuses to start without an AuthKey from keymaster.beammp.com, which only the server owner can get. Until then the adapter has passed unit tests on a mock of BeamMP's Lua API only.
Server side only: BeamNG.drive client mods are out of scope, and no game client is run.
HTTP, and so online license checks, needs curl on the server's PATH.

environments.name: FiveM
environments.platformRulesNote: The platform's creator terms keep paid server content on its own marketplace (Rockstar Games Creator Platform License Agreement, 2026-09-10, §3.1(6)).
environments.blockedOn: Waiting for a server key: FXServer does not start without a Cfx.re registration key (sv_licenseKey).

integration.summary: FiveM already runs this resource shape. `scriptgo pack --target fivem` emits a resource folder with a generated `fxmanifest.lua` and one shared shim file, loaded first, that maps `ScriptGo.*` onto FiveM natives. Threads, events and exports stay FiveM's own.

protection.note: No licence check in the shim, so a package runs there without one. Releases are still signed.

environments.summary: Scripts on FiveM servers, packed as regular FiveM resources.

capabilityNotes.commands: RegisterCommand; restricted commands check the ACE command.<name>.
capabilityNotes.config: Server side: the convar <resource>:<key> (set in server.cfg).
capabilityNotes.events: FiveM's own events and exports; TriggerEvent runs its handlers at once instead of on the next tick.
capabilityNotes.http: Server side, through PerformHttpRequest; redirects are not followed. No host allow-list: the server owner decides what a resource may call.
capabilityNotes.licensing: Not implemented: the shim has no licence check. It was written without one after Rockstar's Creator Platform License Agreement (2026-09-10, §3.1(6)), which forbids a third-party marketplace that sells or licenses server content.
capabilityNotes.logging: print to the server console (channel script:<resource>) or the client console, with the level in front.
capabilityNotes.perks: Not switched on: the shim does not carry the core's perks module.
capabilityNotes.permissions: Server side: ACE (IsPlayerAceAllowed), granted with add_ace in server.cfg.
capabilityNotes.players: Server side: GetPlayers, GetPlayerName, and the license: identifier.
capabilityNotes.presence: The shim answers a player's address (GetPlayerEndpoint) for later use, but it does not carry the core's perks or presence modules, and FiveM's Lua has no HMAC.
capabilityNotes.storage: Resource KVP (GetResourceKvpString / SetResourceKvp) on both sides, values stored as JSON text.
capabilityNotes.ui: Chat messages (chat:addMessage, handled by FXServer's chat system resource).

limitations: Planned: no run on a real FXServer has passed yet. FXServer does not start without a Cfx.re registration key (sv_licenseKey).
No licence check: `scriptgo pack --target fivem` refuses a package that needs one (`licensed true`, or the licensing capability), because the shim could not enforce it.
Only the server half can be verified; the client half needs the game.
`require` finds no resource module on FiveM: list every module as a script.
The client has no `os`: ScriptGo.time.now() is nil there.
RedM runs the same shim (game rdr3); it is not built or verified yet.
